paper_information.title: Identification and Management of Nutrient Disorders and Diseases in Rice: A Visual Diagnostic Tool
paper_information.journal_or_source: Central Rice Research Institute, Indian Council of Agricultural Research, Cuttack 753006, Odisha, India
paper_information.abstract_summary: This visual diagnostic tool and management guide is designed to help researchers, extension workers, students, and farmers identify, understand, and manage nutrient deficiencies, toxicities, and major diseases in rice crops.
paper_information.research_objective: To provide a visual diagnostic tool and management guide for identifying and managing nutrient deficiencies, toxicities, and major diseases in rice.
important_findings: Visual symptoms are often the only immediate diagnostic means available to farmers in the field.
Nutrient stress predisposes plants to various pathogenic diseases.
Proper nutrition enhances chemical, biological, and genetic control of plant pathogens.

general: Water soaked lesions move from tip to downwards on the edges of leaves
Gradually, symptoms turn into yellow and straw coloured stripes with wavy margins
In Kresek (wilt) phase, leaves roll completely, droop and plants die completely
early_symptoms: Symptoms start appearing from the tip and progress downwards in the form of inverted 'V' shape
advanced_symptoms: Affected grains have discoloured spots surrounded by water soaked areas
visual_field_symptoms: BLB infected rice field shows yellow and straw coloured stripes on the sides of the leaves starting from tip

field_identification: Inverted V shape symptom on leaves
Ooze test: a yellowish, opaque, turbid drop of bacterial ooze comes out from cut edge of infected leaf when immersed in water
differential_diagnosis: Late season potassium deficiency resembles BLB, but BLB yields bacterial ooze in water test

cultural_management: Balanced fertilizer application with split application of N
Potash application
Alternate drying and flooding in the field help in reducing infection
biological_management: Spray fresh cow dung extracts (1 kg cow dung in 5 liter water)

chemical_management.application_method: seed soaking in 2 liters of water

chemical_management.active_ingredient_or_product: plantomycin or streptocycline + copper oxy chloride
chemical_management.dose: plantomycin @ 1 g L-1 of water or (streptocycline (0.15g) + copper oxy chloride (1 g) per liter of water)

prevention: Treat seed by soaking in water containing streptocycline and captan
Hot water seed treatment at 53 deg C for 30 min after 12 hrs soak
farmer_action_points: Perform ooze test by cutting leaf and immersing in water

general: Spots appear in the leaves and glumes, seedlings, sheaths, stems and grains
Infected seedlings have small, circular or oval, brown lesions
Fully developed lesion on older leaves is oval, brown with gray or whitish center with reddish brown margin
Black or dark lesions with a velvety aspect develop on glumes
Black discoloration or brown lesions appear on grains
Black discoloration of roots
advanced_symptoms: Under severe infection, lesions may coalesce, killing large areas of affected leaves
Seedlings become stunted or die under severe infestation
visual_field_symptoms: Severely infected plant showing oval, brown spot with gray/whitish center with reddish brown margin

field_identification: Small, circular, dark brown lesions on leaves
differential_diagnosis: Potassium deficient plants show brown spots in older leaves, but spots are dusky without any distinct margin

cultural_management: Use healthy seeds from disease free crops
Adopt deep summer ploughing
Apply balanced NPK with zinc and manganese
Apply additional K (20% extra) at appearance of disease

chemical_management.active_ingredient_or_product: propiconazole or mancozeb or ziram or carbendazim
chemical_management.dose: propiconazole @ 1 mL L-1 or 0.4% mancozeb or 0.25% ziram or 0.2% carbendazim

prevention: Treat seeds with captan or thiram

general: Disease occurs at all crop stages (nursery, tillering, flowering)
Elliptical or spindle shaped lesions with brown border and grayish/ashy center on leaves
Collar region marked by rusty brown appearance at junction of leaf blade and leaf sheath
Stems turn dark brown to blackish color at node (Node blast)
Black necrotic lesions around the base of panicles resulting in breakdown of panicles and formation of chaffy grains (Neck blast)
advanced_symptoms: Under favorable conditions, lesions enlarge and coalesce and entire leaf withers
Entire leaf blade dries up in collar blast
Stem becomes weak and breaks easily in node blast
visual_field_symptoms: Spindle shaped lesions on leaves with brown border and grayish centre

field_identification: Spindle-shaped leaf lesions with gray centers

causes_and_risk_factors: Soils rich in N / fields applied with excess N

cultural_management: Use healthy seeds collected from disease free crops
Apply balanced dose of nitrogenous fertilizer in 3-4 splits (80 kg N ha-1)
Weed out alternate hosts (Cynodron sp. and Paspalum sp.)
Maintain standing water in the field
biological_management: Bael leaf extract (25 g fresh leaves L-1 water)
Tulsi leaf extract (25 g fresh young leaves L-1 water)
Neem leaf extract (200 g fresh leaves L-1 water)

general: Small, dark-green and water-soaked streaks between veins from tillering to booting stage
Streaks enlarge to become yellowish gray and translucent then turn light brown or yellowish brown
Large areas of leaf may become dry due to numerous streaks
early_symptoms: Small dark-green water-soaked streaks between veins
visual_field_symptoms: Patch of yellowish gray interveinal streaks on early infected leaf

field_identification: Bacterial exudates from infected cut leaves when placed in water
differential_diagnosis: Potassium deficiency starts from leaf tip and margin and progresses toward midrib, whereas BLS is interveinal streaks
At later stage indistinguishable from BLB, but BLB has inverted V shape appearance

cultural_management: Apply balanced dose of NPK
Additional potash application in the field helps in reducing infection
Avoid field to field irrigation
Avoid clipping of seedlings at transplanting
biological_management: Spray fresh cow dung extract (1 kg cow dung in 5 liters water) thrice at eight days interval

chemical_management.application_method: seed soaking in 2 liters of water

chemical_management.timing: upon onset of symptoms, twice at 8 days interval

prevention: Hot water treatment of seeds for 12 hours at 53 deg C for 30 minutes

general: Appears in later growth stages in late tillering or early internode elongation stage
Initial symptoms on sheaths of lower leaves or just below leaf collar near water line as small, ellipsoidal or ovoid, greenish-gray and water-soaked lesions
Later lesions occur with grayish white center and light brown to dark brown margin
White sclerotia of mustard seed size found on infected sheaths
early_symptoms: Small, ellipsoidal or ovoid, greenish-gray and water-soaked lesions on lower leaf sheaths
advanced_symptoms: Lesions dry and become grayish-white to tan with brownish borders and may coalesce forming bigger lesions, causing death of whole leaf
Severely infected plants produce poorly filled or empty grains, especially on lower portion of panicles
visual_field_symptoms: Rice plant showing sheath blight lesions on leaf sheath
Rice plant showing sheath blight lesions with brownish border and grayish white centre

field_identification: Ellipsoidal lesions on sheaths with grayish-white centers and dark brown margins

other_conditions: early heading and grain filling stages favor rapid development

cultural_management: Adopt deep summer ploughing so sclerotia in soil are exposed to hot sunlight
Incorporate green manure (Sesbania sp.) in sheath blight endemic areas
Do not transplant more than 3 seedlings hill-1
Maintain field sanitation by removing weeds

general: Freshly emerged leaves exhibit interveinal chlorosis
Leaves gradually turn pale yellow and later reddish orange in color
Plants get stunted and numbers of tillers are reduced
Impaired root growth
early_symptoms: Freshly emerged leaves exhibit interveinal chlorosis
advanced_symptoms: At maturity stage, panicles do not exert completely
visual_field_symptoms: Infected rice plant with reddish orange leaves
Stunted plants with pale yellow leaves in an infected field

field_identification: Occurs as patches within a field, affecting single hills rather than the whole field
Orange-yellow discoloration of leaves and stunting
differential_diagnosis: Symptoms of K deficiency are similar to tungro virus disease, but K deficiency affects the whole field uniformly whereas tungro occurs as patches affecting single hills

cultural_management: Avoid late planting (beyond 2nd week of August) in Eastern Indian states
Clean out weeds like C. rotundus, H. compressa, Hydrolia Zeylanica and Phyllanthus niruri from surrounding of rice fields

prevention: Avoid late planting beyond 2nd week of August in Eastern Indian states

paper_level_notes: The publication is a visual diagnostic tool and management guide for nutrient disorders and major diseases in rice published by the Central Rice Research Institute (ICAR), Cuttack, India in 2013.
